title: Why Multi-Interest Fairness Matters: Hypergraph Contrastive Multi-Interest Learning for Fair Conversational Recommender System

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluated using quantitative fairness metrics for recommender systems, specifically Average Popularity (A@K), Gini Coefficient (G@K), KL-Divergence (L@K), and Difference (D@K), to measure item exposure inequality, the Matthew effect, and preference bias.

Assessed by measuring the system's ability to recommend a diverse set of items that cater to multiple user interests rather than homogeneously recommending only highly relevant or popular items, quantified through the aforementioned distribution metrics.
